title: El Pañuelo de Jalpan, VISTA STORIES
comment: panuelo-jalpan (VISTA): época, finales del siglo XIX, patio de una hacienda en Jalpan, Querétaro. Vestuario de época civil (sin uniformes). Caras comunes, no famosas; los tres se distinguen a simple vista.

chars.ANASTASIO_ECHEVERRIA: Mexican man, proud and feared hacienda owner in the 1890s, 60 years old, fair skin, grey hair combed back with pomade, thick grey sideburns and a grey mustache, hard grey eyes, a black 19th-century frock coat over a grey silk waistcoat and a white high-collar shirt with a black cravat, a gold watch chain on the waistcoat, his hands empty.
chars.MARIANA_ECHEVERRIA: Mexican woman, the hacienda owner's daughter in the 1890s, 22 years old, fair skin, dark-brown hair in an elegant 19th-century updo with a few loose curls, large dark eyes, a pale-blue 19th-century high-necked long-sleeve dress with white lace at the collar and cuffs, small pearl earrings, her hands empty.
chars.MATIAS_ROBLEDO: Mexican mestizo man, the hacienda administrator in the 1890s, 30 years old, warm brown skin, short black hair, a neat black mustache, honest dark eyes, a simple brown wool 19th-century jacket over a white cotton shirt without collar, a brown waistcoat, dark trousers, a wide-brimmed palm hat in his hand, his hands otherwise empty.

locs.LOC_HACIENDAJALPAN: Inner courtyard of an old 19th-century hacienda in Jalpan, Sierra Gorda of Queretaro, in the soft late afternoon: ochre and white walls, a stone fountain in the center, arched corridors with heavy wooden doors, potted geraniums, green mountains of the Sierra Gorda beyond the roofs, no modern objects, no readable text, no signs, no logos, no people.
